#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Validate the Brand Architect pack and spawn template.

The template is a thinking overlay for brand-system Sol managers. It cannot be
spawned as the master persona, a Luna worker, or a default for every manager.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SCHEMA = "company-os.brand-architect-spawn-template.v1"
TEMPLATE_ID = "brand-architect"
REQUIRED_SKILLS = ("manage-company-program", "brand-architect")
FORBIDDEN_ROLES = ("master", "worker")
USE_WHEN = (
    "brand_governance",
    "brand_identity",
    "brand_presence",
    "brand_system",
    "brand_voice",
    "positioning",
)
SOURCE_FILES = (
    "00-index.txt",
    "01-brand-system-strategy-framework.txt",
    "02-positioning-category-differentiation.txt",
    "03-target-audience-intelligence.txt",
    "04-brand-pillars-identity-credibility-visibility.txt",
    "05-storytelling-emotional-appeal.txt",
    "06-visual-identity-logo-color-typography.txt",
    "07-brand-voice-messaging-system.txt",
    "08-experience-principles-delivery-design.txt",
    "09-brand-presence-social-distribution.txt",
    "10-governance-architecture-equity-expansion.txt",
)
TOP_LEVEL = {
    "schema",
    "template_id",
    "role",
    "requested_model",
    "skills",
    "forbidden_roles",
    "source_pack",
    "authority",
    "use_when",
}
SKILL_MARKERS = (
    "brand-system sol managers",
    "do not send this skill to luna workers",
    "do not use it as the master persona",
    "does not own",
    "every major claim needs proof",
)


def validate_pack(root: Path = ROOT) -> list[str]:
    errors: list[str] = []
    skill = root / "SKILL.md"
    if not skill.is_file():
        return ["missing SKILL.md"]
    text = skill.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if not text.startswith("---\nname: brand-architect\n"):
        errors.append("SKILL.md name must be brand-architect")
    words = len(text.split())
    if words > 700:
        errors.append(f"SKILL.md exceeds 700 words: {words}")
    folded = text.casefold()
    for marker in SKILL_MARKERS:
        if marker not in folded:
            errors.append(f"SKILL.md missing required marker: {marker}")
    if "TODO" in text:
        errors.append("SKILL.md has unresolved TODO")

    source_root = root / "references" / "source"
    for name in SOURCE_FILES:
        path = source_root / name
        if not path.is_file() or path.stat().st_size <= 0:
            errors.append(f"missing source file: {name}")
    extra = sorted(
        path.name
        for path in source_root.iterdir()
        if path.is_file() and path.name not in SOURCE_FILES
    )
    if extra:
        errors.append(f"unexpected source files: {', '.join(extra)}")

    for host in ("openai.yaml", "grok.yaml"):
        host_path = root / "agents" / host
        if not host_path.is_file():
            errors.append(f"missing agents/{host}")
            continue
        host_text = host_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        if "$brand-architect" not in host_text:
            errors.append(f"agents/{host} must invoke the skill")
        if "allow_implicit_invocation: false" not in host_text:
            errors.append(f"agents/{host} must disable implicit invocation")

    template_path = root / "assets" / "spawn-template.json"
    if not template_path.is_file():
        errors.append("missing spawn template")
    else:
        try:
            payload = json.loads(template_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, UnicodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            errors.append("spawn template is unreadable JSON")
        else:
            errors.extend(validate_spawn_template(payload))
    return errors


def validate_spawn_template(payload: Any) -> list[str]:
    errors: list[str] = []
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        return ["spawn template must be an object"]
    extra = sorted(set(payload) - TOP_LEVEL)
    missing = sorted(TOP_LEVEL - set(payload))
    if extra:
        errors.append(f"unknown spawn keys: {', '.join(extra)}")
    if missing:
        errors.append(f"missing spawn keys: {', '.join(missing)}")
    if payload.get("schema") != SCHEMA:
        errors.append(f"schema must be {SCHEMA}")
    if payload.get("template_id") != TEMPLATE_ID:
        errors.append("template_id drifted")
    if payload.get("role") != "manager":
        errors.append("spawn role must be manager")
    if payload.get("requested_model") != "gpt-5.6-sol":
        errors.append("requested_model must remain gpt-5.6-sol")
    if payload.get("authority") != "thinking_overlay":
        errors.append("authority must be thinking_overlay")
    if payload.get("source_pack") != "references/source":
        errors.append("source_pack drifted")
    skills = payload.get("skills")
    if not isinstance(skills, list) or list(skills) != list(REQUIRED_SKILLS):
        errors.append("spawn skills must be the manager role skill plus brand-architect")
    forbidden = payload.get("forbidden_roles")
    if not isinstance(forbidden, list) or set(forbidden) != set(FORBIDDEN_ROLES):
        errors.append("forbidden_roles must be master and worker")
    use_when = payload.get("use_when")
    if not isinstance(use_when, list) or list(use_when) != list(USE_WHEN):
        errors.append("use_when must be the brand-system lanes")
    return errors


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=ROOT)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    errors = validate_pack(args.root)
    print(json.dumps({"valid": not errors, "errors": errors}, indent=2))
    return 0 if not errors else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Brand and Creative System

Create a single, living expression system rather than disconnected copy or visual polish.

When a Sol manager owns this lane, load `$brand-architect` as the
brand-architecture overlay and `$steve` as the product-taste overlay. This
skill remains the brand operating contract. Do not send either overlay to Luna
workers.

## Operating contract

Capture the audience, category tension, point of view, promise, proof, personality, visual/motion principles, language rules, and prohibited patterns. Distinguish evidence from creative conviction. Do not invent customer claims, logos, legal claims, or brand assets.

## Workflow

1. **Extract:** inspect approved project artifacts, product behavior, customer language, and market context; label unknowns.
2. **Frame:** create a concise brand thesis: who the product is for, the before/after, why it is uniquely credible, and the emotional standard.
3. **Systematize:** define message hierarchy, vocabulary, visual/motion behaviors, accessibility constraints, and reusable content patterns.
4. **Apply:** make only additive, reversible changes consistent with the existing product language unless an audited defect warrants a redesign.
5. **Audit:** challenge every artifact for clarity, distinctiveness, truthfulness, accessibility, cohesion, and customer fit. Link evidence and reject surface novelty.

## Creative quality gate

Score each applicable dimension from 1–10 with direct evidence: strategic clarity, distinctiveness, customer relevance, product truth, visual cohesion, interaction/motion purpose, accessibility, readability, adaptability, and legal/claim safety. A customer-facing stage is no-go below 9 on any critical dimension or if its claims lack substantiation.

## Authority

Agents can analyze, propose, and create internal drafts. Require approval before publishing, changing a production interface, using protected assets, or making external claims.

## Handoff

Write the current brand thesis, evidence, unresolved tensions, approved rules, rejected directions, artifact locations, score, and exact next safe action into the shared ledger.

# Build Outcome Evaluators

Missing evaluation capability is a build problem, not permission to remove the quality gate.

## Compile evaluator build work

```bash
python3 skills/company-os/build-outcome-evaluators/scripts/compile_evaluator_build_fabric.py \
  --project-root /absolute/project \
  --evaluator-contract .company-os/outcomes/viral-game/runtime/evaluator-contract.json \
  --artifact-contract .company-os/outcomes/viral-game/runtime/artifact-contract.json \
  --benchmark-contract .company-os/outcomes/viral-game/runtime/benchmark-contract.json \
  --output .company-os/outcomes/viral-game/runtime/evaluator-build-fabric.json
```

The compiler finds required `workspace://` adapters whose entrypoint files do not yet exist. It assigns each missing evaluator to a disjoint worker scope at the exact adapter path. A batch contains at most six evaluator workers under the existing bounded two manager legacy fabric. If more remain, run the next batch after the first is materialized and registered.

## Worker contract

Each worker receives the exact evaluator definition and the bound artifact and benchmark contract paths. It must inspect `$execute-outcome-evaluator`, implement the required adapter input and output protocol, and prove that the adapter can emit every required evidence type and score dimension. The adapter must judge actual artifact behavior for its modalities. Source inspection or a production completion narrative cannot substitute for required interaction, visual, audio, runtime, or other experiential evidence.

If a real external runtime is required and unavailable, return the exact prerequisite as a blocker. Do not fake evidence.

After workers finish, run `$register-outcome-evaluators`. Calibration remains mandatory before production scale.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compile bounded work for missing required outcome evaluator adapters."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
from typing import Any, Mapping

CONTRACT_SCHEMA = "company-os.evaluator-runtime-contract.v1"
ARTIFACT_SCHEMA = "company-os.artifact-observation-contract.v1"
BENCHMARK_SCHEMA = "company-os.benchmark-contract.v1"
WORKSPACE_PREFIX = "workspace://"
PHASES = ["charter", "discovery", "design", "execution", "verification", "integration"]
MAX_BATCH = 6


class BuildFabricError(ValueError):
    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str) -> None:
        self.code = code
        self.message = message
        super().__init__(f"{code}: {message}")


def text(value: Any, label: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip() or "\x00" in value:
        raise BuildFabricError("E_SCHEMA", f"{label} must be nonempty")
    return value.strip()


def obj(value: Any, label: str) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
    if not isinstance(value, Mapping):
        raise BuildFabricError("E_SCHEMA", f"{label} must be an object")
    return value


def load_module(path: Path, name: str):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
        raise BuildFabricError("E_RUNTIME", f"cannot load {name}")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def company_root() -> Path:
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


def repo_root() -> Path:
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]


def control_store_module():
    return load_module(
        company_root() / "elastic-company-os/scripts/control_store.py",
        "company_os_build_evaluator_store",
    )


def fabric_module():
    return load_module(
        repo_root() / "skills/autonomy-suite/orchestration/luna-execution-fabric/scripts/validate_fabric.py",
        "company_os_build_evaluator_fabric",
    )


def read_json(path: Path, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        raw = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        raise BuildFabricError("E_JSON", f"cannot read {label}: {path}") from exc
    return dict(obj(raw, label))


def verify_contract(raw: Mapping[str, Any], schema: str, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    value = dict(raw)
    if value.get("$schema") != schema:
        raise BuildFabricError("E_SCHEMA", f"{label} must use {schema}")
    if value.get("ready") is not True:
        raise BuildFabricError("E_NOT_READY", f"{label} is not ready")
    return value


def workspace_relative(locator: Any, label: str) -> str:
    locator = text(locator, label)
    if not locator.startswith(WORKSPACE_PREFIX):
        raise BuildFabricError(
            "E_UNBUILDABLE_LOCATOR",
            f"{label} is not a project local workspace adapter",
        )
    raw = locator[len(WORKSPACE_PREFIX) :]
    pure = PurePosixPath(raw)
    if (
        not raw
        or "\\" in raw
        or pure.is_absolute()
        or not pure.parts
        or any(part in {"", ".", ".."} for part in pure.parts)
    ):
        raise BuildFabricError("E_PATH", f"{label} workspace path is unsafe")
    return pure.as_posix()


def missing_required(
    project_root: Path,
    evaluator_contract: Mapping[str, Any],
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    records = evaluator_contract.get("evaluators")
    if not isinstance(records, list):
        raise BuildFabricError("E_SCHEMA", "evaluator contract evaluators must be an array")
    missing = []
    root = project_root.resolve()
    for raw in records:
        if not isinstance(raw, Mapping) or raw.get("required") is not True:
            continue
        evaluator = dict(raw)
        evaluator_id = text(evaluator.get("evaluator_id"), "evaluator_id")
        relative = workspace_relative(
            evaluator.get("adapter_locator"),
            f"{evaluator_id}.adapter_locator",
        )
        candidate = root / Path(*PurePosixPath(relative).parts)
        if candidate.exists():
            if candidate.is_symlink() or not candidate.is_file():
                raise BuildFabricError(
                    "E_PATH", f"existing evaluator adapter is not a regular file: {relative}"
                )
            continue
        evaluator["entrypoint"] = relative
        missing.append(evaluator)
    return sorted(missing, key=lambda item: str(item.get("evaluator_id", "")))


def worker_task(
    evaluator: Mapping[str, Any],
    *,
    evaluator_contract_path: str,
    artifact_contract_path: str,
    benchmark_contract_path: str,
) -> str:
    evaluator_id = evaluator["evaluator_id"]
    return (
        f"Build the missing required Company OS evaluator adapter {evaluator_id!r} at the exact path "
        f"{evaluator['entrypoint']!r}. Inspect the local execute outcome evaluator runtime and implement its "
        "company-os.evaluator-adapter-input.v1 to company-os.evaluator-adapter-output.v1 protocol. "
        f"The exact evaluator definition is {json.dumps(dict(evaluator), sort_keys=True)}. "
        f"Read the bound evaluator contract {evaluator_contract_path!r}, artifact contract {artifact_contract_path!r}, "
        f"and benchmark contract {benchmark_contract_path!r}. The adapter must evaluate actual artifacts in classes "
        f"{sorted(evaluator.get('artifact_classes', []))}, produce every required evidence type "
        f"{sorted(evaluator.get('produces_evidence', []))}, and return every score dimension "
        f"{sorted(evaluator.get('score_dimensions', []))}. Evidence files must be real project files produced by the "
        "evaluation. Do not grade source code when the artifact contract requires interactive, visual, audio, runtime, "
        "or other experiential observation. Do not modify the product candidate. If the required external runtime or "
        "tooling is unavailable, return that exact prerequisite as a blocker instead of fabricating evidence."
    )


def compile_manifest(
    project_root: Path,
    evaluator_contract_path: str,
    artifact_contract_path: str,
    benchmark_contract_path: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    project_root = project_root.resolve()
    evaluator_contract = verify_contract(
        read_json(project_root / evaluator_contract_path, "evaluator contract"),
        CONTRACT_SCHEMA,
        "evaluator contract",
    )
    artifact_contract = verify_contract(
        read_json(project_root / artifact_contract_path, "artifact contract"),
        ARTIFACT_SCHEMA,
        "artifact contract",
    )
    benchmark_contract = verify_contract(
        read_json(project_root / benchmark_contract_path, "benchmark contract"),
        BENCHMARK_SCHEMA,
        "benchmark contract",
    )
    objective_id = text(evaluator_contract.get("objective_id"), "objective_id")
    if artifact_contract.get("objective_id") != objective_id or benchmark_contract.get("objective_id") != objective_id:
        raise BuildFabricError("E_BINDING", "outcome runtime contracts do not share one objective")
    missing = missing_required(project_root, evaluator_contract)
    batch = missing[:MAX_BATCH]
    remaining = [item["evaluator_id"] for item in missing[MAX_BATCH:]]
    if not batch:
        return {
            "complete": True,
            "objective_id": objective_id,
            "missing_evaluator_ids": [],
            "remaining_evaluator_ids": [],
            "fabric": None,
        }
    try:
        _, state = control_store_module().load(project_root)
    except Exception as exc:
        raise BuildFabricError(
            "E_STATE", f"Company OS transactional control store is required: {exc}"
        ) from exc
    strategy = obj(state.get("strategy"), "strategy")
    project_id = text(obj(state.get("instance"), "instance").get("project_id"), "project_id")
    program_version = strategy.get("program_version")
    if not isinstance(program_version, int) or isinstance(program_version, bool) or program_version < 1:
        raise BuildFabricError("E_STATE", "strategy.program_version is invalid")

    program_outcome = f"Materialize missing independent evaluator adapters for objective {objective_id}"
    manager_groups = [batch[index : index + 3] for index in range(0, len(batch), 3)]
    managers = []
    for manager_index, group in enumerate(manager_groups, 1):
        manager_id = f"evaluator-builder-manager-{manager_index:02d}"
        manager_scope = f".company-os/evaluator-build/batch/{manager_index:02d}"
        manager_outcome = f"Build and verify evaluator adapters for {[item['evaluator_id'] for item in group]}"
        workers = []
        for worker_index, evaluator in enumerate(group, 1):
            entrypoint = evaluator["entrypoint"]
            parent = str(PurePosixPath(entrypoint).parent)
            task = worker_task(
                evaluator,
                evaluator_contract_path=evaluator_contract_path,
                artifact_contract_path=artifact_contract_path,
                benchmark_contract_path=benchmark_contract_path,
            )
            workers.append(
                {
                    "id": f"{manager_id}-worker-{worker_index:02d}",
                    "model": "gpt-5.6-luna",
                    "task": task,
                    "acceptance": [
                        f"Adapter exists at {entrypoint}",
                        "Adapter is valid Python and imports without syntax errors",
                        "Adapter implements the exact evaluator adapter input and output schemas",
                        "Adapter returns every required score dimension",
                        "Adapter produces every required evidence type as actual files",
                        "Adapter does not mutate production candidate artifacts",
                    ],
                    "write_scope": [parent],
                    "risk": "medium",
                    "budget": {
                        "time_minutes": 30.0,
                        "token_limit": 8000,
                        "cost_usd": 8.0,
                        "max_concurrency": 1,
                        "max_retries": 1,
                    },
                    "outcome_context": {
                        "program_version": program_version,
                        "north_star": strategy.get("north_star") or "Produce independently verified outcomes",
                        "user_value": f"Executable evaluator capability for {objective_id}",
                        "program_outcome": program_outcome,
                        "manager_outcome": manager_outcome,
                        "roadmap_position": "execution",
                        "dependencies": [
                            evaluator_contract_path,
                            artifact_contract_path,
                            benchmark_contract_path,
                            "skills/company-os/execute-outcome-evaluator/scripts/execute_evaluator.py",
                        ],
                        "non_goals": ["Modify product candidate artifacts", "Lower evaluator requirements"],
                        "constraints": [
                            "Independent evaluator capability cannot trust production narrative",
                            "Required experiential evidence cannot be replaced by source inspection",
                            "Fabrication of unavailable evidence is forbidden",
                        ],
                    },
                    "stop_condition": "The adapter is real and executable, or a concrete unavailable prerequisite is proven.",
                }
            )
        managers.append(
            {
                "id": manager_id,
                "model": "gpt-5.6-sol",
                "outcome": manager_outcome,
                "acceptance": [
                    "Every assigned adapter path exists or has an explicit prerequisite blocker",
                    "No evaluator requirement was weakened",
                    "Worker changes remain inside disjoint evaluator adapter scopes",
                ],
                "phase_ids": PHASES,
                "budget": {
                    "time_minutes": 120.0,
                    "token_limit": 30000,
                    "cost_usd": 30.0,
                    "max_concurrency": 1,
                    "max_retries": 1,
                },
                "write_scope": [manager_scope, *sorted({worker["write_scope"][0] for worker in workers})],
                "workers": workers,
            }
        )
    worker_count = sum(len(manager["workers"]) for manager in managers)
    fabric = {
        "program_id": project_id,
        "program_version": program_version,
        "outcome": program_outcome,
        "acceptance": [
            "All adapters in this batch are materialized or expose exact external prerequisites",
            "Required evaluator contract semantics are preserved",
            "Adapters are ready for content addressed registration and calibration",
        ],
        "program_contract": {
            "north_star": strategy.get("north_star") or "Produce independently verified outcomes",
            "user_value": f"Independent quality judgment for {objective_id}",
            "rationale": "The outcome loop cannot judge reality until required evaluator capabilities exist.",
            "architecture": "Bounded adapter construction workers implement exact evaluator runtime contracts in disjoint workspace scopes.",
            "roadmap": PHASES,
            "dependencies": [evaluator_contract_path, artifact_contract_path, benchmark_contract_path],
            "non_goals": ["Production candidate modification", "Quality gate removal"],
            "constraints": ["No fabricated evidence", "No evaluator self grading by production workers"],
        },
        "max_managers": len(managers),
        "max_manager_concurrency": len(managers),
        "max_workers_per_manager": 3,
        "max_total_workers": worker_count,
        "max_depth": 2,
        "max_worker_retries": 1,
        "max_manager_rework_rounds": 2,
        "budget": {
            "time_minutes": 360.0,
            "token_limit": 90000,
            "cost_usd": 90.0,
            "max_concurrency": len(managers),
            "max_retries": 1,
        },
        "luna_token_share_target": 0.75,
        "external_effects_allowed": False,
        "managers": managers,
    }
    validation = fabric_module().validate(fabric)
    if not validation.get("valid"):
        raise BuildFabricError("E_FABRIC", "; ".join(validation.get("errors", [])))
    return {
        "complete": False,
        "objective_id": objective_id,
        "missing_evaluator_ids": [item["evaluator_id"] for item in batch],
        "remaining_evaluator_ids": remaining,
        "fabric": fabric,
    }


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--project-root", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--evaluator-contract", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--artifact-contract", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--benchmark-contract", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        result = compile_manifest(
            args.project_root,
            args.evaluator_contract,
            args.artifact_contract,
            args.benchmark_contract,
        )
        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    "ok": True,
                    "complete": result["complete"],
                    "missing_evaluator_ids": result["missing_evaluator_ids"],
                    "remaining_evaluator_ids": result["remaining_evaluator_ids"],
                },
                sort_keys=True,
            )
        )
        return 0
    except BuildFabricError as exc:
        print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "code": exc.code, "error": exc.message}, sort_keys=True))
        return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":

# Business Architect

This is a thinking overlay for business-architecture Sol managers. It does not own authority, leases, fabric, or completion. `$manage-company-program`, `$strategy-pillar`, and `$portfolio-direction` still win.

This doctrine is an original compiled operating template stored with its source pack. It is not a claim of personal identity, private knowledge, quoted speech, or affiliation with McKinsey, Porter, Jobs, or Strategyzer.

Do not send this skill to Luna workers. Do not use it as the master persona. Do not attach it to a manager whose outcome is not business model, competitive strategy, value proposition, jobs-to-be-done, or market analysis.

## Every heartbeat

Before dispatching business-architecture work, answer these:

1. Name the decision. A canvas without a decision is decoration.
2. Pick one primary framework. Do not stack all seventeen invokers.
3. Never invent business facts. Mark assumptions and the test that would falsify them.
4. Keep one customer, job, or segment unless the framework is industry-level.
5. Pause if this is a canvas without a decision, a strategy without a constraint, or a metric without a customer-value link.

Do not invent customers, TAM, legal conclusions, or competitor facts. Do not authorize campaigns, offers, CRM, HRIS, scheduler, or runtime changes from this overlay.

## Forced moves

- Lean Canvas for early or uncertain work; Business Model Canvas when the model is more known.
- Value Proposition Canvas is one segment only. JTBD uses: When [situation], I want to [motivation], so I can [outcome].
- Industry tools stay at industry level. Do not fake firm-level Five Forces or PESTEL data.
- North Star must reflect customer value and carry guardrails.
- Name the bottleneck and the cheapest test that would kill the model.
- Do not enable the Company OS scheduler or runtime from this overlay.

## Artifacts

Keep these manager-local and compact:

- named decision and chosen framework
- filled canvas or force map with assumptions ledger
- bottleneck, risks, and falsifying tests
- one leading metric with guardrails when a metric is the decision

## Source pack

Load only the file needed. Do not paste the pack into worker prompts.

| Need | File |
| --- | --- |
| Business model | `references/source/business-model-canvas.txt` |
| Early / uncertain | `references/source/lean-canvas.txt` |

file_name: business_model_canvas_invoker.txt
purpose: >
  A reusable, invoke-anytime .txt blueprint that lets the user paste a business description
  (or minimal inputs) and receive a complete, high-quality Business Model Canvas (BMC)
  plus assumptions, risks, tests, and next actions.
how_to_use:
  overview: >
    This file is meant to be copied into your agent system or prompt library.
    When you want a Business Model Canvas, you paste:
    1) the contents of this file (as system or prepended context),
    2) then a short "BUSINESS INPUT" section describing the business.
  invocation_phrases:
    - "Invoke BMC"
    - "Build the Business Model Canvas"
    - "BMC for: <business name>"
  expected_output_artifacts:
    - "Business Model Canvas (9 blocks) written in crisp bullets"
    - "Assumptions ledger (what must be true)"
    - "Risk and bottleneck analysis"
    - "Validation plan (tests, metrics, time boxes)"
    - "30/60/90 execution plan with owners and KPIs"
    - "Optional: unit economics and pricing sensitivity"
operating_rules:
  scope_control:
    rule: >
      Never invent business facts. If the user does not provide a detail,
      explicitly mark it as an assumption and propose 2–4 plausible options.
  no_clarifying_questions_default:
    rule: >
      Do not ask clarifying questions unless the business cannot be modeled at all.
      Instead, produce a best-effort BMC using assumptions and show them.
  precision:
    rule: >
      Prefer specific mechanisms: who pays, why they pay, how they discover,
      how fulfillment works, what the bottleneck is, and what the leading metric is.
  format:
    rule: >
      Use headings for each BMC block. Use short bullets. Add a dedicated
      "Assumptions" subsection under each block when needed.
input_contract:
  user_input_template: |
    BUSINESS INPUT
    Name:
    One-liner:
    Type: (SaaS, ecom, marketplace, agency, app, media, etc.)
    Target customer:
    Primary problem:
    Current stage: (idea, MVP, revenue, scaling)
    Offer(s):
    Pricing (if known):
    Acquisition channels (if known):
    Fulfillment/delivery:
    Differentiation:
    Constraints: (budget, time, skills, geography, compliance)
    Current metrics (if any):
  minimum_viable_input:
    description: >
      If the user provides only a name + one-liner, the invoker must still build a canvas by:
      1) selecting a likely business type from context,
      2) choosing default customer segments and channels consistent with that type,
      3) marking everything else as assumptions with test plans.
output_spec:
  section_order:
    - "1. Business Snapshot"
    - "2. Business Model Canvas"
    - "3. Assumptions Ledger"
    - "4. Unit Economics (if applicable)"
    - "5. Bottlenecks and Risks"
    - "6. Validation and Experiments"
    - "7. Execution Plan (30/60/90)"
    - "8. Optional Variants (alt canvases)"
  depth_standard:
    business_snapshot:
      includes:
        - "Core thesis: why this wins"
        - "Primary customer and job-to-be-done"
        - "Moat hypothesis"
        - "Main constraint"
        - "Single leading KPI"
    bmc_block_depth:
      instruction: >
        Each block must include:
        - Core bullets (what it is)
        - Mechanics (how it works in practice)
        - Metrics (how to measure it)
        - Assumptions (explicit)
        - Failure modes (what breaks it)
business_snapshot_logic:
  core_thesis_framework:
    formula: >
      "We win because [customer] has [urgent problem] and current alternatives fail due to
      [gap]. Our offer delivers [quantified outcome] via [mechanism], distributed through
      [channel], with retention driven by [loop/moat]."
  leading_kpi_selector:
    rules:
      - "SaaS: activation rate, WAU/MAU, net revenue retention, CAC:LTV"
      - "Ecom: contribution margin per order, repeat rate, MER"
      - "Marketplace: liquidity metrics, take rate, GMV, time-to-match"
      - "Agency: gross margin, utilization, sales cycle length, churn"
business_model_canvas:
  key_partners:
    intent: >
      External entities that reduce cost/risk, increase reach, or enable delivery.
    include:
      - "Supplier stack (data, infra, manufacturers, payment processors)"
      - "Distribution partners (affiliates, platforms)"
      - "Credibility partners (certifications, influencers, associations)"
      - "Strategic complements (bundles, integrations)"
    mechanics_prompts:
      - "What do we buy vs build?"
      - "Who has the audience we need?"
      - "Where do we borrow trust?"
    metrics:
      - "Partner-sourced revenue %"
      - "Partner CAC vs direct CAC"
      - "Dependency risk score"
    failure_modes:
      - "Single point of failure dependency"
      - "Channel conflict"
      - "Partner incentives misaligned"
  key_activities:
    intent: >
      The few actions that must be done exceptionally well to deliver value and grow.
    include:
      - "Product creation and iteration loop"
      - "Demand generation and conversion"
      - "Fulfillment and customer success"
      - "Operations and quality control"
    mechanics_prompts:
      - "What are the 2–3 activities that create 80% of value?"
      - "What activities compound over time?"
    metrics:
      - "Cycle time (idea→ship)"
      - "Conversion rate by funnel stage"
      - "Support tickets per customer"
    failure_modes:
      - "Too many activities, no focus"
      - "Non-scalable manual steps"
  key_resources:
    intent: >
      The assets required to make the model work.
    categories:
      physical: ["inventory", "equipment", "warehouses"]

file_name: core_context_framework_invoker.txt
framework: Core–Context Framework

purpose: >
  Distinguish between activities that create competitive advantage (Core)
  and those that are necessary but non-differentiating (Context),
  to optimize resource allocation and execution focus.

definitions:
  core:
    description: >
      Activities that directly drive competitive advantage,
      differentiation, and long-term value creation.
    characteristics:
      - strategically_unique
      - hard_to_copy
      - value_driving
  context:
    description: >
      Activities required to run the business but not sources
      of differentiation.
    characteristics:
      - necessary
      - operational
      - easily_outsourced

classification_rules:
  questions:
    - "Does this activity create customer-perceived differentiation?"
    - "Would losing excellence here destroy advantage?"
    - "Can competitors replicate this easily?"

outputs:
  - core_activities
  - context_activities
  - invest_or_optimize_decisions
  - outsource_or_automate_recommendations

file_name: decision_tree_journal_invoker.txt
framework: Decision Tree and Decision Journal

purpose: >
  Improve decision quality by separating decision logic from outcomes
  and reducing hindsight bias.

decision_tree:
  components:
    - decision_options
    - probabilities
    - expected_values
    - downside_risk

decision_journal:
  required_fields:
    - date
    - decision_context
    - assumptions
    - expected_outcomes
    - confidence_level

review_process:
  timing:
    - 30_days
    - 90_days
    - 1_year
  evaluation:
    - outcome_vs_expectation
    - assumption_accuracy

file_name: flywheel_model_invoker.txt
framework: Flywheel Model

purpose: >
  Identify and design self-reinforcing growth loops
  that compound advantage over time.

flywheel_definition:
  description: >
    A flywheel is a closed-loop system where outputs
    reinforce inputs, increasing momentum with each cycle.

components:
  nodes:
    description: Key activities or outcomes in the loop.
  links:
    description: How one node strengthens the next.

design_rules:
  principles:
    - "Customer value must increase each cycle"
    - "Friction must be reduced continuously"
    - "Momentum compounds non-linearly"

analysis_outputs:
  - flywheel_diagram_nodes
  - reinforcing_loops
  - friction_points
  - compounding_metrics

file_name: four_actions_framework_invoker.txt

purpose: >
  A reusable, invoke-anytime Four Actions Framework used to reconstruct
  industry value curves and drive value innovation.
  This file preserves the canonical ERRC format while extending it into
  cost discipline, differentiation logic, and execution planning.

what_this_is:
  definition: >
    The Four Actions Framework challenges an industry’s strategic logic
    by asking four questions:
    What should be eliminated, reduced, raised, and created?
  primary_goal: >
    Break the value–cost tradeoff by eliminating and reducing low-value
    factors while raising and creating high-value ones.
  not_this:
    - "A feature wishlist"
    - "A brainstorming exercise without tradeoffs"
    - "An optimization-only tool"

canonical_format:
  quadrants:
    - Eliminate
    - Reduce
    - Raise
    - Create
  invariant_rule: >
    True strategy requires tradeoffs.
    If nothing is eliminated or reduced, there is no strategy.

spatial_logic:
  cost_side:
    description: "Eliminate and Reduce lower cost structure"
  value_side:
    description: "Raise and Create increase buyer value"
  strategic_balance: >
    The framework must rebalance cost and value simultaneously.

invocation_rules:
  invocation_phrases:
    - "Invoke Four Actions Framework"
    - "Run ERRC grid"
    - "Four Actions for <business / product / industry>"
  no_questions_default:
    rule: >
      Do not ask clarifying questions by default.
      Generate a best-effort ERRC grid using assumptions where required.
  discipline_constraint:
    rule: >
      Each item must reference a real industry factor or activity.

input_contract:
  user_input_template: |
    FOUR ACTIONS INPUT
    Business / Product:
    Industry:
    Target Customer:
    Strategy Intent: (cost leadership / differentiation / value innovation)
    Competitive Context:
    Evidence Available: (none, customer data, market data)
  minimum_viable_input:
    description: >
      If only an industry is provided,
      infer standard competitive factors and industry norms
      and mark all inferred items as assumptions.

output_spec:
  section_order:
    - "1. Scope and Strategic Intent"
    - "2. Four Actions Grid"
    - "3. Cost–Value Impact Assessment"
    - "4. Assumptions Ledger"
    - "5. Risks and Failure Modes"
    - "6. Strategic Initiatives"
    - "7. Review Cadence"

scope_and_strategic_intent:
  rules:
    - "One industry and customer context"
    - "Explicit strategic intent"
  why_this_matters: >
    ERRC grids collapse when multiple customer contexts are mixed.
    Precision is structural.

four_actions_grid:

  eliminate:
    definition: >
      Factors the industry has long competed on
      that no longer add meaningful value to customers.
    guiding_questions:
      - "What do customers not care about?"
      - "What exists only because competitors do it?"
    impact:
      cost: "High reduction potential"
      value: "Minimal or neutral loss"
    failure_modes:
      - "Eliminating table stakes"
      - "Fear-based attachment to legacy features"

  reduce:
    definition: >
      Factors that should be reduced well below industry standard.
    guiding_questions:
      - "Where is the industry over-serving?"
      - "Which factors drive cost without proportional value?"
    impact:
      cost: "Moderate reduction"
      value: "Acceptable tradeoff"
    failure_modes:
      - "Reducing differentiators"
      - "Reducing without customer validation"

  raise:
    definition: >
      Factors that should be raised well above industry standard.
    guiding_questions:
      - "Where are customers forced to compromise?"
      - "Which factors disproportionately influence choice?"
    impact:
      cost: "Targeted increase"
      value: "High perceived benefit"
    failure_modes:
      - "Raising too many factors"
      - "Raising factors customers don’t notice"

  create:
    definition: >
      New factors the industry has never offered.
    guiding_questions:
      - "What would eliminate customer pain entirely?"
      - "What new sources of value could unlock demand?"
    impact:
      cost: "Selective increase"
      value: "New demand creation"
    failure_modes:
      - "Novelty without value"
      - "Creation without feasibility"

cost_value_impact_assessment:
  evaluation_dimensions:
    cost_effect:
      scale: "Decrease / Neutral / Increase"
    value_effect:
      scale: "Decrease / Neutral / Increase"
  prioritization_rule: >
    Favor actions that increase value while decreasing or neutralizing cost.
  warning_signal: >
    If most actions increase cost, strategy coherence is weak.

assumptions_ledger:
  categories:
    customer_value_assumptions:
      description: "Beliefs about what customers truly value"
    cost_assumptions:
      description: "Beliefs about cost savings or increases"
    competitor_response_assumptions:
      description: "Beliefs about how competitors will react"
    adoption_assumptions:
      description: "Beliefs about customer switching behavior"

risks_and_failure_modes:
  strategic:
    - "No real tradeoffs"
    - "Incrementalism disguised as innovation"
  execution:
    - "Cost structure incompatible with raised or created factors"
    - "Inability to deliver promised value"
  cognitive:
    - "Anchoring to industry norms"
    - "Internal bias toward complexity"

strategic_initiatives:
  output_definition: >
    Concrete initiatives derived from ERRC actions.
  examples:
    - "Remove legacy feature set to simplify operations"
    - "Reduce service tiers to cut overhead"
    - "Raise onboarding quality to accelerate adoption"
    - "Create a new value dimension competitors ignore"
  success_metrics:
    - "Customer switching rate"
    - "Margin improvement"
    - "Reduced price sensitivity"

review_cadence:
  recommended:
    stable_industries: "Annual"
    dynamic_industries: "Quarterly"
  trigger_events:
    - "Competitive convergence"
    - "Cost pressure"
    - "Customer behavior shift"

file_name: jobs_to_be_done_invoker.txt
framework: Jobs To Be Done

purpose: >
  Identify the real causal drivers of customer behavior by understanding
  the progress customers are trying to make.

job_structure:
  job_statement:
    format: "When [situation], I want to [motivation], so I can [outcome]."

forces_of_progress:
  push:
    description: Pain with the current situation.
  pull:
    description: Attraction to a new solution.
  anxiety:
    description: Concerns about adopting something new.
  habit:
    description: Inertia keeping the customer in place.

analysis_outputs:
  - primary_job
  - competing_alternatives
  - switching_triggers
  - adoption_barriers

file_name: lean_canvas_invoker.txt

purpose: >
  A reusable, invoke-anytime Lean Canvas definition for early-stage,
  uncertainty-heavy businesses.
  This canvas is optimized for speed, learning, and risk reduction.

what_this_is:
  definition: >
    The Lean Canvas is a startup-focused adaptation of the Business Model Canvas.
    It replaces long-term infrastructure thinking with problem-solution
    and traction-first thinking.
  best_used_when:
    - "Idea stage"
    - "Pre-PMF"
    - "Early revenue"
    - "High uncertainty environments"
  not_for:
    - "Mature enterprises"
    - "Highly regulated, slow-cycle industries without modification"

canonical_format:
  structure:
    top_row:
      - Problem
      - Solution
      - Unique Value Proposition
      - Unfair Advantage
      - Customer Segments
    middle_row:
      - Key Metrics
      - Channels
    bottom_row:
      - Cost Structure
      - Revenue Streams
  invariant_rule: >
    The Unique Value Proposition sits at the center.
    Everything else supports or validates it.

spatial_logic:
  left_side: Problem Space
  center: Value Hypothesis
  right_side: Market & Distribution
  bottom: Economics
  execution_focus: >
    The canvas is read as a set of hypotheses to be tested,
    not facts to be defended.

invocation_rules:
  invocation_phrases:
    - "Invoke Lean Canvas"
    - "Build Lean Canvas for <startup>"
    - "Lean Canvas for <idea>"
  no_questions_default:
    rule: >
      Do not ask clarifying questions by default.
      Produce a best-effort canvas using explicit assumptions.
  bias_toward_action:
    rule: >
      Prefer speed and falsifiability over completeness.

input_contract:
  user_input_template: |
    LEAN CANVAS INPUT
    Startup / Product Name:
    One-liner:
    Target Customer:
    Primary Problem:
    Existing Alternatives:
    Stage: (idea, MVP, revenue)
    Pricing (if known):
    Distribution ideas (if known):
    Constraints:
    Evidence available: (none, interviews, usage, revenue)
  minimum_viable_input:
    description: >
      If only a name or idea is provided,
      infer the rest from first principles and
      mark all inferred elements as assumptions.

output_spec:
  section_order:
    - "1. Canvas Scope"
    - "2. Lean Canvas Blocks"
    - "3. Assumptions Ledger"
    - "4. Riskiest Assumptions"
    - "5. Failure Modes"
    - "6. Validation Plan"
    - "7. Iteration Strategy"

canvas_scope:
  rules:
    - "One primary customer segment"
    - "One core problem"
    - "One core solution"
  why_this_matters: >
    Lean Canvas breaks when it tries to serve everyone.
    Focus is a structural requirement.

lean_canvas_blocks:

  problem:
    definition: >
      The top 1–3 problems the customer urgently cares about.
    rules:
      - "Problems must be painful and frequent"
      - "Phrase in customer language"
      - "Avoid solution framing"
    include:
      - "Existing alternatives or workarounds"
    metrics:
      - "Problem frequency"
      - "Customer frustration intensity"
    failure_modes:
      - "Nice-to-have problems"
      - "Founder-only problems"

  solution:
    definition: >
      A high-level description of how you solve the problem.
      Not a feature list.
    rules:
      - "One solution per problem cluster"
      - "Assume solution is wrong until proven"
    maturity_levels:
      - "Concept"
      - "MVP"
      - "V1"
    metrics:
      - "Time to first value"
      - "Adoption rate"
    failure_modes:
      - "Overbuilt solution"
      - "Solution in search of problem"

  unique_value_proposition:
    definition: >
      A single, clear statement that explains why this product matters
      and why it is different.
    formula: >
      "For [customer] who [problem], our product is [category]
      that [primary benefit], unlike [alternative]."
    rules:
      - "Clear > clever"
      - "Outcome-focused"
    metrics:
      - "Message resonance"
      - "Conversion lift"
    failure_modes:
      - "Buzzwords"
      - "Feature-based UVP"

  unfair_advantage:
    definition: >
      Something that cannot be easily copied or bought.
      If none exists, say 'none yet'.
    examples:
      - "Founder insight"
      - "Exclusive data"
      - "Distribution leverage"
      - "Brand trust"
      - "Network effects"
    rules:
      - "If it can be copied in 6 months, it’s not unfair"
    metrics:
      - "Defensibility over time"
    failure_modes:
      - "Claiming future advantages as current"
      - "Generic advantages"

  customer_segments:
    definition: >
      The specific people who experience the problem.
    include:
      - "Early adopters"
      - "Decision-makers vs users"
    rules:
      - "Narrow before broad"
      - "Segment by behavior, not demographics"
    metrics:
      - "Activation rate by segment"
    failure_modes:
      - "Everyone as a customer"

  key_metrics:
    definition: >
      The few numbers that tell you if the business is working.
    rules:
      - "Avoid vanity metrics"
      - "Metrics should drive decisions"
    examples_by_type:
      SaaS:
        - "Activation rate"
        - "Retention"
        - "MRR growth"
      ecom:
        - "Contribution margin"
        - "Repeat purchase rate"
      marketplace:
        - "Liquidity"
        - "Time to match"
    failure_modes:
      - "Tracking too many metrics"

  channels:
    definition: >
      How you reach and acquire customers.
    categories:

file_name: mckinsey_7s_framework_invoker.txt

purpose: >
  A reusable, invoke-anytime McKinsey 7S Framework used to diagnose
  organizational alignment and execution capability.
  This file preserves the canonical 7S model while extending it into
  actionable decisions, risks, and change initiatives.

what_this_is:
  definition: >
    The McKinsey 7S Framework evaluates how seven internal elements of an
    organization align to support strategy and performance.
  primary_goal: >
    Identify misalignment that prevents strategy from being executed.
  not_this:
    - "A market analysis"
    - "A financial model"
    - "A culture-only assessment"

canonical_format:
  elements:
    hard_elements:
      - Strategy
      - Structure
      - Systems
    soft_elements:
      - Shared Values
      - Style
      - Staff
      - Skills
  invariant_rule: >
    All seven elements must be aligned.
    Optimizing one in isolation degrades overall performance.

spatial_logic:
  center:
    shared_values: "The core beliefs and purpose at the heart of the organization"
  dependency_logic: >
    Hard elements are easier to change.
    Soft elements determine sustainability.
  diagnostic_principle: >
    Performance problems usually arise from misalignment, not incompetence.

invocation_rules:
  invocation_phrases:
    - "Invoke McKinsey 7S"
    - "Run 7S analysis"
    - "7S for <organization / team / initiative>"
  no_questions_default:
    rule: >
      Do not ask clarifying questions by default.
      Perform a best-effort diagnosis using assumptions where necessary.
  honesty_constraint:
    rule: >
      Do not sanitize cultural or leadership issues.
      Soft elements must be assessed directly.

input_contract:
  user_input_template: |
    7S INPUT
    Organization / Initiative:
    Stage: (early, scaling, mature, turnaround)
    Strategy Summary:
    Org Size:
    Leadership Structure:
    Known Issues (if any):
    Evidence Available: (none, anecdotes, metrics)
  minimum_viable_input:
    description: >
      If only an organization or initiative name is provided,
      infer typical 7S patterns for the stage and industry
      and mark all inferred items as assumptions.

output_spec:
  section_order:
    - "1. Scope and Context"
    - "2. The 7S Elements"
    - "3. Alignment Assessment"
    - "4. Assumptions Ledger"
    - "5. Misalignment Risks"
    - "6. Change Initiatives"
    - "7. Review Cadence"

scope_and_context:
  rules:
    - "One organization or unit per 7S"
    - "Explicit time horizon"
  why_this_matters: >
    7S diagnoses are time-sensitive.
    Alignment today may not hold after growth or change.

seven_s_elements:

  strategy:
    definition: >
      The plan for achieving competitive advantage and long-term goals.
    evaluation_questions:
      - "Is the strategy clear and explicit?"
      - "Is it differentiated?"
      - "Is it understood beyond leadership?"
    metrics:
      - "Strategic clarity"
      - "Execution consistency"
    failure_modes:
      - "Implicit or outdated strategy"
      - "Strategy disconnected from reality"

  structure:
    definition: >
      How roles, responsibilities, and authority are organized.
    evaluation_questions:
      - "Does structure support the strategy?"
      - "Are decision rights clear?"
    metrics:
      - "Decision latency"
      - "Span of control"
    failure_modes:
      - "Over-centralization"
      - "Conflicting reporting lines"

  systems:
    definition: >
      The processes and workflows that drive daily operations.
    evaluation_questions:
      - "Do systems reinforce desired behavior?"
      - "Are incentives aligned?"
    metrics:
      - "Process cycle time"
      - "Error or rework rate"
    failure_modes:
      - "Manual workarounds"
      - "Metrics that drive the wrong behavior"

  shared_values:
    definition: >
      Core beliefs, purpose, and norms that guide behavior.
    evaluation_questions:
      - "Are values explicit or implicit?"
      - "Are they lived or only stated?"
    metrics:
      - "Cultural consistency"
      - "Value-behavior alignment"
    failure_modes:
      - "Stated values contradict incentives"
      - "Cultural drift during growth"

  style:
    definition: >
      Leadership approach and management behavior.
    evaluation_questions:
      - "How do leaders actually behave?"
      - "What behavior is rewarded or punished?"
    metrics:
      - "Psychological safety"
      - "Speed of escalation"
    failure_modes:
      - "Command-and-control mismatch"
      - "Avoidance of accountability"

  staff:
    definition: >
      The people, their roles, and overall workforce composition.
    evaluation_questions:
      - "Are the right people in the right roles?"
      - "Is talent scaling with strategy?"
    metrics:
      - "Retention"
      - "Role clarity"
    failure_modes:
      - "Talent gaps"
      - "Misaligned incentives"

  skills:
    definition: >
      The capabilities and competencies the organization does well.
    evaluation_questions:
      - "What are we uniquely good at?"
      - "Which skills are missing?"
    metrics:
      - "Skill coverage"
      - "Learning velocity"
    failure_modes:
      - "Outdated core skills"
      - "Skills misaligned with strategy"

alignment_assessment:
  method:
    description: >
      Evaluate pairwise alignment between elements.
  critical_pairs:
    - "Strategy ↔ Structure"
    - "Strategy ↔ Skills"
    - "Systems ↔ Shared Values"
    - "Style ↔ Staff"
  scoring:
    scale: "Low / Medium / High alignment"
  diagnostic_rule: >
    One low-alignment pair can negate strengths elsewhere.

assumptions_ledger:
  categories:
    strategy_assumptions:
      description: "Beliefs about competitive positioning"
    leadership_assumptions:
      description: "Beliefs about management behavior"
    culture_assumptions:
      description: "Beliefs about values in practice"
    capability_assumptions:
      description: "Beliefs about skills depth"

misalignment_risks:
  common_patterns:
    - "Strategy changed, structure did not"
    - "Growth outpaced systems"
    - "Values diluted during scaling"
    - "Leadership style misfit for stage"

change_initiatives:
  principles:
    - "Fix alignment before adding complexity"
    - "Change hard elements to influence soft elements"
  examples:
    - "Redesign decision rights to support strategy"
    - "Update incentives to reinforce values"
    - "Invest in capability building"
  success_metrics:
    - "Execution speed"
    - "Consistency of behavior"

review_cadence:
  recommended:
    early_stage: "Every 6 months"
    scaling: "Annually"
    mature: "Annually or during transformation"
  trigger_events:
    - "Rapid growth"
    - "Leadership change"
    - "Strategic pivot"

file_name: pestel_analysis_invoker.txt

purpose: >
  A reusable, invoke-anytime PESTEL Analysis framework used to evaluate
  macro-environmental forces that affect a business, market, or industry.
  This file preserves the canonical PESTEL format while extending it into
  decision-ready strategic insights.

what_this_is:
  definition: >
    PESTEL Analysis examines six macro-environmental dimensions:
    Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Environmental, and Legal.
  scope: >
    PESTEL focuses on forces outside the firm’s direct control.
    It informs strategy, risk management, and timing decisions.
  not_this:
    - "A competitive analysis"
    - "An internal capability assessment"

canonical_format:
  dimensions:
    - Political
    - Economic
    - Social
    - Technological
    - Environmental
    - Legal
  invariant_rule: >
    All factors must be external to the firm.
    Internal reactions belong in strategy, not in PESTEL.

spatial_logic:
  macro_to_micro:
    description: >
      PESTEL scans the environment broadly,
      then filters down to what materially affects the business.
  time_horizon:
    default: "12–36 months"
    note: "Some factors evolve slowly; others move suddenly."

invocation_rules:
  invocation_phrases:
    - "Invoke PESTEL"
    - "Run PESTEL analysis"
    - "PESTEL for <business / industry / market>"
  no_questions_default:
    rule: >
      Do not ask clarifying questions by default.
      Produce a best-effort PESTEL using assumptions where needed.
  relevance_constraint:
    rule: >
      Exclude factors that do not materially affect decisions.

input_contract:
  user_input_template: |
    PESTEL INPUT
    Business / Industry:
    Geography:
    Stage: (early, scaling, mature)
    Time Horizon:
    Regulatory Exposure (low / medium / high):
    Evidence Available: (none, reports, data)
  minimum_viable_input:
    description: >
      If only an industry or business name is provided,
      infer relevant PESTEL factors for the geography
      and mark all inferred elements as assumptions.

output_spec:
  section_order:
    - "1. Scope and Context"
    - "2. PESTEL Factors"
    - "3. Assumptions Ledger"
    - "4. Impact & Uncertainty Assessment"
    - "5. Strategic Implications"
    - "6. Priority Watchlist"
    - "7. Review Cadence"

scope_and_context:
  rules:
    - "One geography per PESTEL"
    - "Explicit time horizon"
  why_this_matters: >
    Macro forces vary significantly by country and over time.
    Mixing geographies or horizons reduces signal quality.

pestel_factors:

  political:
    definition: >
      Government actions, policies, and political stability factors.
    examples:
      - "Tax policy"
      - "Trade restrictions"
      - "Government stability"
      - "Subsidies or incentives"
    impact_vectors:
      - "Cost structure"
      - "Market access"
    metrics:
      - "Policy volatility"
      - "Government intervention likelihood"
    failure_modes:
      - "Ignoring local vs national differences"
      - "Overreacting to short-term noise"

  economic:
    definition: >
      Macroeconomic conditions affecting purchasing power and costs.
    examples:
      - "Interest rates"
      - "Inflation"
      - "Employment levels"
      - "Currency fluctuations"
    impact_vectors:
      - "Demand elasticity"
      - "Cost of capital"
    metrics:
      - "GDP growth"
      - "Consumer spending trends"
    failure_modes:
      - "Assuming stable macro conditions"
      - "Ignoring second-order effects"

  social:
    definition: >
      Demographic, cultural, and behavioral trends.
    examples:
      - "Demographic shifts"
      - "Lifestyle changes"
      - "Consumer attitudes"
      - "Trust and values"
    impact_vectors:
      - "Product adoption"
      - "Brand perception"
    metrics:
      - "Adoption rate by cohort"
      - "Cultural alignment risk"
    failure_modes:
      - "Projecting founder values onto market"
      - "Ignoring slow-moving social change"

  technological:
    definition: >
      Technological developments that affect products, processes, or markets.
    examples:
      - "Automation"
      - "AI adoption"
      - "Platform evolution"
      - "Infrastructure changes"
    impact_vectors:
      - "Cost reduction"
      - "New business models"
    metrics:
      - "Rate of tech adoption"
      - "Obsolescence risk"
    failure_modes:
      - "Chasing hype cycles"
      - "Ignoring build vs buy tradeoffs"

  environmental:
    definition: >
      Ecological and sustainability-related factors.
    examples:
      - "Climate regulations"
      - "Resource availability"
      - "Energy costs"
    impact_vectors:
      - "Compliance costs"
      - "Supply chain stability"
    metrics:
      - "Environmental compliance burden"
      - "Resource volatility"
    failure_modes:
      - "Treating sustainability as PR only"
      - "Ignoring supply-side risks"

  legal:
    definition: >
      Laws and regulations governing how business is conducted.
    examples:
      - "Labor laws"
      - "Data protection"
      - "Industry-specific regulation"
    impact_vectors:
      - "Operational constraints"
      - "Liability exposure"
    metrics:
      - "Regulatory change frequency"
      - "Compliance cost"
    failure_modes:
      - "Underestimating enforcement"
      - "Assuming regulations are static"

assumptions_ledger:
  categories:
    policy_assumptions:
      description: "Beliefs about political or regulatory direction"
    macro_assumptions:
      description: "Beliefs about economic stability"
    behavior_assumptions:
      description: "Beliefs about consumer or societal change"
    technology_assumptions:
      description: "Beliefs about adoption speed"

impact_and_uncertainty_assessment:
  scoring_dimensions:
    impact:
      scale: "Low / Medium / High"
    uncertainty:
      scale: "Low / Medium / High"
  prioritization_rule: >
    Focus strategy on factors with High Impact and High Uncertainty.

strategic_implications:
  strategy_types:
    exploit:
      description: "Use favorable trends to accelerate growth"
    hedge:
      description: "Reduce exposure to adverse forces"
    wait:
      description: "Delay commitment until uncertainty resolves"
  rule: >
    PESTEL insights must translate into timing,
    investment, or risk-mitigation decisions.

priority_watchlist:
  definition: >
    A short list of macro factors to monitor continuously.
  output_limit:
    max_items: 5
  failure_modes:
    - "Monitoring everything"
    - "Monitoring nothing"

review_cadence:
  recommended:
    stable_industries: "Annual"
    volatile_industries: "Quarterly"
  trigger_events:
    - "Regulatory change"
    - "Macroeconomic shock"
    - "Technological inflection"

file_name: porters_five_forces_invoker.txt
framework: Porter's Five Forces

purpose: >
  Analyze the structural attractiveness and long-term profitability

forces:
  threat_of_new_entrants:

  bargaining_power_of_suppliers:

  bargaining_power_of_buyers:

  threat_of_substitutes:

file_name: promise_model_invoker.txt

purpose: >
  A reusable, invoke-anytime Promise Model used to define,
  operationalize, and defend a business’s core promise.
  This framework ensures alignment between what is promised,
  how it is delivered, and how trust is maintained over time.

what_this_is:
  definition: >
    The Promise Model defines the explicit and implicit commitments
    a business makes to customers and ensures the organization is
    structurally capable of delivering them consistently.
  primary_goal: >
    Eliminate the gap between expectation and reality.
  not_this:
    - "A brand slogan exercise"
    - "A positioning statement only"
    - "A marketing copy framework"

canonical_format:
  core_components:
    - Promise
    - Delivery System
    - Proof
  invariant_rule: >
    A promise without delivery destroys trust.
    Delivery without proof is invisible.
    Proof without a clear promise is meaningless.

spatial_logic:
  flow:
    promise: "Sets expectation"
    delivery: "Fulfills expectation"
    proof: "Confirms expectation"
  trust_loop: >
    Promise → Delivery → Proof → Reinforced Trust → Repeat

invocation_rules:
  invocation_phrases:
    - "Invoke Promise Model"
    - "Build Promise Model for <business / product>"
    - "Define the core promise"
  no_questions_default:
    rule: >
      Do not ask clarifying questions by default.
      Build a best-effort Promise Model using assumptions where required.
  integrity_constraint:
    rule: >
      Never inflate the promise beyond delivery capability.

input_contract:
  user_input_template: |
    PROMISE MODEL INPUT
    Business / Product:
    Target Customer:
    Core Outcome Customer Wants:
    Competitive Context:
    Stage: (early, scaling, mature)
    Known Strengths:
    Known Constraints:
    Evidence Available: (none, anecdotes, metrics)
  minimum_viable_input:
    description: >
      If only a business or product name is provided,
      infer a realistic promise based on industry norms
      and mark all inferred elements as assumptions.

output_spec:
  section_order:
    - "1. Scope and Customer Context"
    - "2. The Promise"
    - "3. Delivery System"
    - "4. Proof Mechanisms"
    - "5. Promise–Delivery Fit Assessment"
    - "6. Assumptions Ledger"
    - "7. Failure Modes"
    - "8. Reinforcement Strategy"

scope_and_customer_context:
  rules:
    - "One primary customer segment"
    - "One core promise"
  why_this_matters: >
    Multiple promises dilute trust.
    Customers remember broken promises more than kept ones.

promise:
  definition: >
    A clear, outcome-focused commitment to the customer.
  characteristics:
    - "Specific"
    - "Outcome-oriented"
    - "Time-bound where possible"
    - "Emotionally resonant but operationally grounded"
  formulation_rules:
    - "State the outcome, not the method"
    - "Avoid superlatives unless provable"
  examples:
    strong:
      - "Reduce onboarding time by 50% within 30 days"
    weak:
      - "Best-in-class experience"
  failure_modes:
    - "Overpromising"
    - "Vague or abstract promises"

delivery_system:
  definition: >
    The internal mechanisms that reliably fulfill the promise.
  components:
    people:
      description: "Roles, skills, and accountability"
    process:
      description: "Repeatable workflows and standards"
    technology:
      description: "Tools and systems enabling delivery"
    governance:
      description: "Decision rights and escalation paths"
  alignment_rule: >
    Every element of the delivery system must map directly
    to fulfilling the promise.
  metrics:
    - "Delivery consistency"
    - "Time-to-outcome"
  failure_modes:
    - "Manual heroics instead of systems"
    - "Misaligned incentives"

proof:
  definition: >
    Observable evidence that the promise has been fulfilled.
  types:
    functional:
      description: "Measured outcomes or performance data"
    social:
      description: "Testimonials, reviews, case studies"
    behavioral:
      description: "Retention, referrals, repeat usage"
  rules:
    - "Proof must be visible to the customer"
    - "Proof should be timely"
  metrics:
    - "Customer-reported outcomes"
    - "Retention and advocacy"
  failure_modes:
    - "Hidden proof"
    - "Unverifiable claims"

promise_delivery_fit_assessment:
  evaluation_questions:
    - "Can we deliver this promise 90% of the time?"
    - "What breaks first under scale?"
    - "What happens if demand doubles?"
  fit_levels:
    weak:
      description: "Promise exceeds delivery capability"
    aligned:
      description: "Promise and delivery are matched"
    conservative:
      description: "Delivery exceeds promise"

assumptions_ledger:
  categories:
    customer_expectation_assumptions:
      description: "Beliefs about what customers expect"
    capability_assumptions:
      description: "Beliefs about operational capacity"
    perception_assumptions:
      description: "Beliefs about what customers notice"
    scaling_assumptions:
      description: "Beliefs about delivery at scale"

failure_modes:
  strategic:
    - "Promise creep over time"
    - "Marketing-driven promises"
  operational:
    - "Inconsistent delivery"
    - "No ownership of the promise"
  reputational:
    - "Broken trust"
    - "Negative word-of-mouth"

reinforcement_strategy:
  internal:
    actions:
      - "Train teams on the promise"
      - "Tie incentives to promise fulfillment"
  external:
    actions:
      - "Reinforce proof in customer touchpoints"
      - "Close the loop with customers"
  review_cadence:
    recommended:
      early_stage: "Quarterly"
      scaling: "Biannual"
      mature: "Annual"
